skill.name: workflow-automation
skill.description: Design durable workflow automation with clear platform choices, orchestration patterns, retries, checkpoints, and observability for reliable agent and backend systems.
skill.summary: Plan reliable workflows using n8n, Temporal, Inngest, and durable execution patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 68 uses Markdown backticks to format related skill names, not Ruby or shell execution. The file is prompt documentation only and contains no executable code path.

content.value_statement: Unreliable scripts fail when long processes hit retries, outages, or partial completion. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design durable workflows with clear platform choices and production safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Compare n8n, Temporal, and Inngest for workflow automation decisions.
Explain sequential, parallel, and orchestrator-worker workflow patterns.
Identify risks in payment, background job, and scheduled task workflows.
Recommend durability controls such as checkpoints, retries, timeouts, and idempotency.
Outline observability needs for production workflows and agent systems.
limitations: Does not include executable automation templates or platform SDK code.
Does not inspect live workflow systems, logs, queues, or cloud accounts.
Requires user-provided requirements to choose the best platform accurately.
Cannot guarantee platform pricing, limits, or current feature availability.

use_cases.title: Select an Automation Platform
use_cases.description: Compare n8n, Temporal, and Inngest against team skills, reliability needs, and operational constraints.

use_cases.title: Plan Durable Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Design workflows that recover from failed steps, external API outages, and partial completion.

use_cases.title: Review Background Job Architecture
use_cases.description: Find weak points in job queues, scheduled tasks, retries, timeouts, and observability coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between n8n, Temporal, and Inngest for this workflow: [describe workflow]. Compare reliability, complexity, team fit, and operations.

prompt_templates.title: Map Workflow Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this process into a durable workflow design: [describe process]. Identify sequential steps, parallel steps, checkpoints, retries, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this workflow architecture for production risks: [paste design]. Focus on idempotency, timeouts, observability, data size, and recovery behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Orchestrator-Worker System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an orchestrator-worker workflow for [business process]. Include worker boundaries, retry rules, state ownership, monitoring, and escalation paths.

output_examples.input: A team needs to automate invoice approvals with human review and retries.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a durable workflow with approval checkpoints, retryable notifications, idempotent accounting updates, and audit visibility.

output_examples.input: A startup asks whether n8n or Temporal fits a payment workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare accessibility against correctness, then warn that payment flows need idempotency, durable state, timeouts, and clear recovery.

output_examples.input: An AI agent runs a 12-step customer onboarding process.
output_examples.output: The skill would break the process into durable steps, isolate external calls, add checkpoints, and define failure handling for each stage.

best_practices: Use idempotency keys for external calls that may be retried.
Break long workflows into checkpointed steps with clear recovery behavior.
Add timeouts, backoff, and observability before running workflows in production.
anti_patterns: Do not run payment workflows as brittle scripts without durable state.
Do not place every business process inside one large monolithic workflow.
Do not ship workflows without logs, metrics, alerts, and failure ownership.

faq.question: What platforms does this skill discuss?
faq.answer: It discusses n8n, Temporal, and Inngest, with attention to reliability, complexity, and team fit.

faq.question: Can it generate production workflow code?
faq.answer: It focuses on architecture and review guidance. It does not include ready-made executable templates.

faq.question: Is this useful for AI agent workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps design durable agent workflows that can recover from failures and partial completion.

faq.question: Does it replace platform documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it for design decisions, then verify implementation details in current platform documentation.

faq.question: What workflow risks does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes missing idempotency, weak retries, absent checkpoints, long monolithic workflows, and poor observability.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
